summary: Iteration 5 — Phase 7 (password recovery + security questions via Resend). BACKEND: 23/23 pytest tests pass in /app/backend/tests/test_password_recovery.py covering: GET /auth/security-questions (8 items), GET /auth/security-status auth-guarded + masked email + questions_set, POST /auth/security-setup validation (rejects invalid email, !=2 questions, duplicate qid, <2 char answer, unknown qid; happy-path persists hashed answers + email + masked echo), POST /auth/verify-otp inner user.has_recovery_email & has_security_questions, POST /auth/login-password security_setup_required flag (Priya True, Rohan False), POST /auth/forgot/start (unknown→not_recoverable, Priya→no_recovery_set, Rohan→ok with masked email + 2 questions), POST /auth/forgot/request-code (all-wrong→403, 1-of-2 correct case-insensitive+trim→success with dev_code since Resend rejects non-verified recipients, repeat within 30s→429), POST /auth/forgot/reset (wrong code→403, <6 char password→400, correct dev_code→success, new password works, old rejected, expires_in_minutes=15), and /auth/me redaction (no password_hash/security_questions/reset_code_hash/reset_code_expires_at/reset_code_sent_at/questions_set leaked; raw recovery_email allowed for owner). FRONTEND: 100% pass — /login shows login-forgot-link on password step; clicking goes to /forgot; full 3-step recovery (phone → 2 question answers → dev_code + new password) completes and redirects to /login; Priya (no recovery set) is force-redirected to /security-setup after login (RequireAuth gate works); SecuritySetup form (ss-email-input, ss-pick-1/2 as native SELECTs, ss-ans-1/2, ss-submit-btn) saves and refreshes user → navigates to role home; /settings page renders settings-recovery-card with masked email 'pr********@example.com' and the two configured questions; settings-update-recovery-btn swaps in the SecuritySetup form; nav-settings link present in Layout for sales_manager. NOTE: Master Admin (9873117605) is ALSO force-redirected to /security-setup since recovery was never set on the master — this is per-spec but means admin can't reach the dashboard / webhook-bridge-panel / nav-settings until they complete setup. User should be informed they need to complete master admin's security setup once, or main agent can choose to exempt the master role.

critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/server.py is now ~2561 lines (auth, contacts, agent, provider, webhooks, sync, security, seed all in one file). Strongly recommend splitting into routers (auth_router.py, security_router.py, agent_router.py, provider_router.py, webhooks_router.py, admin_router.py) before the next phase — files >700 lines violate the size guideline.

Forgot-flow rate-limit (30s) is implemented by storing reset_code_sent_at on the user doc and comparing on next /forgot/request-code. Edge case: a user who passes the 30s window but never finishes the reset accumulates expired reset_code_hash; the cleanup happens lazily in forgot/reset only on expiration check. Consider a TTL index on reset_code_expires_at or an explicit $unset when the code expires server-side rather than waiting for the user to call reset.

_send_reset_email_resend returns False on any exception including Resend's 'testing emails only to verified recipient' restriction, and the response always exposes dev_code in that case. This is correctly dev-only behaviour for the test API key in .env, but ensure that when SENDER_EMAIL is moved to a verified custom domain (resend.dev replaced with the real one), dev_code is NEVER returned. Add a unit test guarding: `if email_sent: assert dev_code is None`.

Rate-limit message 'Please wait a few seconds...' returns 429 but doesn't say how many seconds remain — frontend has to guess. Consider returning {retry_after: <int seconds>} in the body so the UI can countdown.

Security answers are hashed individually with bcrypt (1 hash per question) — verify_password runs synchronously inside the request handler. For 2 answers this is fine (~200ms total) but if the question count grows, consider asyncio.to_thread or argon2id.

/auth/security-status returns the question TEXT (good for FE display) but /auth/forgot/start does the same — make sure the question-text-from-id mapping (SECURITY_QUESTION_TEXT) stays stable across deploys, otherwise pre-existing users may see different question text than what they originally answered. Recommend adding a migration check or storing the canonical text on each user's security_questions[i].

ForgotResetBody.code is treated as str then `.strip()`'d before verify — good. But there is no length check on code itself before bcrypt verify (a malicious caller could send a 10MB string and bcrypt will hash it all). Add `if not (4 <= len(data.code) <= 12)` guard before verify_password.

rca of the issue: No new bugs found in Phase 7. The pre-existing iteration_4 issue (sales_rep can hit /api/admin/webhooks/test-send) is still open. The only behavioural quirk worth flagging is that Master Admin is now subject to the same forced /security-setup gate as everyone else because security_setup_required is computed purely from has_recovery_email && has_security_questions — there is no is_master_admin bypass. If that is undesired (master admin can't reach the webhook bridge until they set up recovery), add `or current.get('is_master_admin')` to the security_setup_required check in _safe_user, or skip the RequireAuth-side check when user.is_master_admin === true.
